html:
The Chinantla is the homeland of the Chinantec people, who call themselves Tsa ju jmí', in the mountains and lowland rainforest of northern Oaxaca, Mexico, sloping down toward Veracruz. Their Chinantecan languages belong to the Oto-Manguean family and are among the most tonal in the world; some communities can also whistle their speech across the hills.

Before the Spanish, the Chinantla was divided into small lordships. The Aztec Triple Alliance conquered part of it in the later 1400s and kept a garrison at Tuxtepec, while other Chinantec towns held out. Their neighbours were the Mazatec, the Mixe and the Zapotecs. Under New Spain and after, the region grew tobacco, cotton and later coffee. In the 1970s and 1980s the Cerro de Oro dam flooded part of the lowland Chinantla, and thousands of Chinantec were resettled.
